newsitem.title: USA: Exxon may surprise, most majors seen flat to worse.
newsitem.headline: Exxon may surprise, most majors seen flat to worse.

text.p: Exxon Corp kicks off the rush of oil majors' second quarter earnings on Monday, but any exuberance following a possible upside earnings surprise at the biggest company in the group will quickly evaporate as most majors are seen flat or down.

Most analysts do not see any surprises from the international majors, but one that does is Michael Young at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell who predicts Exxon will report a 16 percent rise in earnings from the year-ago quarter.
He is forecasting $0.75 per share for the second quarter, against a Firt Call consensus of $0.71 and $0.63 a year ago.

"Foreign refining and marketing results are forecast to surge to $300 million versus $134 million in the second quarter of 1996, while U.S. donwstream earnings are projected to be flat at $100 million," Young said.
He says that Exxon is highly leveraged to a decline in feedstock prices and should also perform well in its chemicals operations.

The rest of the group is set to break five successive quarters of improving earnings and Salomon Brothers analyst Paul Ting expects earnings to be down on average 17 percent from the first quarter, due to a $3.00 per barrel decline in oil prices.

Among the international companies, he expects earnings to be in line with consensus, but among the domestics, there could be negative surprises from Amerada Hess, Atlantic Richfield Co and Phillips Petroleum Co.

For Phillips, he believes that its chemical operations, while improving are doing so at a slower rate than its peers and the company could report earnings per share of $0.70, below the $0.80 consensus.

Amerada Hess may break even says Ting, as opposed to coming in line with the $0.33 consensus due to poor downstream earnings, while ARCO's underperformance comes from the fact that it is one of the most heavily reliant on upstream earnings.

Others note that Hess has deferred a $15 million expense associated with North Sea exploration to the third quarter and Eugene Nowak, analyst at ABN Amro has increased his forecast to $0.30 per share.
The outlook for oil prices is poor through the second half, barring some unforseen shock, and share price performance in the sector has already been roiled by the prospects for decline.
"Looking further out for the sector, the macro picture of declining oil prices and the seasonal weakening in the downstream sector does not augur well for the end of the year," said Salomon's Ting.
West Texas Intermediate oil prices averaged $19.98 in the quarter, compared with $23.00 in the first quarter and $21.66 in the year ago quarter, he said.
Spot natural gas prices are also off, at $2.00 per thousand cubic feet from $2.44 per mcf in the first quarter and $2.13 a year ago.
The biggest losers are likely to be those which have a heavy focus on exploration and production.

Schroder & Co analyst Michael Mayer sayd that Unocal Corp will show the largest quarter on quarter decline of all majors, down 45 percent at $0.40 per share compared with $0.76 in he first quarter and $0.79 a year ago.
He notes that the company will take a $0.05 charge against a dry hole drilled in Brunei, which has not yet been taken account of by consensus forecasts.
Texaco Inc will also suffer from its upstream focus and its lack of chemical operations and Mayer is looking for $1.50 per share compared with $1.84 in the first quarter and $1.73 a year ago.
Domestic refining margins have been a mixed bag, up 18 percent on the Gulf Coast, 18 percent on the East Coast and 69 percent in the Midwest, but they declined 22 percent on the West Coast.
Overall, Bear Sterns analyst Fred Leuffer is looking for a 10 percent improvement in refining earnings from the year ago and up 39 percent from the first quarter.

One area of improvement in the current quarter is the chemicals sector, where lower feedstock prices are bolstering margins, but in the fourth quarter largescale new capacity is set to overhang the ethylene industry.
